literal: Those who are detached, they say, are those who are free from desire; others, in that manner, do not have detachment.
translation: Those who are truly detached are those who have freed themselves from desire; all others, though they may have renounced other things, are not truly detached.
modern: பற்றுகளை அறுத்தவர் என்று சொல்லப்படுபவர் ஆசைகளை அறுத்தவரே ஆவர்; மற்றவர்கள் வேறு எவற்றைத் துறந்திருந்தாலும், முழுமையாகத் துறந்தவர்கள் ஆக மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate nature of true renunciation. The poet states that only those who have completely eradicated desire (அவா) can be called truly detached (அற்றவர்). Others (மற்றையார்) might have given up their wealth, family, or worldly possessions, but if they still harbor desire in their minds, they have not achieved complete detachment (அற்றது இலர்). The core message is that desire is the root of all attachment, and renouncing everything else is meaningless if desire itself remains.
